## Summary

Kubernetes v1.35.1 bundles `registry.k8s.io/coredns/coredns:v1.13.1` as the
default DNS provider. The upstream CoreDNS project has since released v1.14.6,
which addresses the vast majority of known vulnerabilities present in v1.13.1.

cluster administrators rely on the officially bundled version, we are requesting
that the CoreDNS version be bumped in an upcoming Kubernetes patch release.

title: Exec readiness probes silently broken during graceful pod termination since v1.35 (probe context canceled at teardown)
description:
### What happened?

Since v1.35.0, exec readiness probes stop working the moment a pod begins graceful termination. Every probe attempt fails client-side with `rpc error: code = Canceled desc = context canceled`, the prober discards errored results, and the pod's `Ready` condition stays frozen at whatever it was before termination began. A pod whose readiness probe starts failing during its grace period is never marked NotReady.

This is a regression from #130487 (`chore(kubelet): migrate prober
resolution: Closed via GitHub issue #140881 in kubernetes/kubernetes (see linked PR/comments for fix details)

title: Pre-Submit Scalability Testing for Agent Sandbox
description:
**What would you like to be added?**

I propose the introduction of a pre-submit check for Pull Requests in the `kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox` repository. This check will trigger scalability tests against the changes in the PR *before* they are merged.

**Why is this needed?**

Currently, scalability testing is done post-submit, which means regressions might only be caught after merging, potentially on a periodic basis. This can delay feedback and make it harder to pinpoint the cause of issues.

When computing a pod's node-allocatable footprint from DRA claims, the scheduler looks up the allocated device by pool name and device name only, and does not consider the driver. A DRA device is identified by `(driver, pool, device)`, so two drivers that publish the same pool name and device name on a node collide, and the lookup can return the wrong driver's device.

title: DRA structured allocator leaks reserved counters and constraints when it rejects or backtracks a candidate device
description:
### What happened?

The structured DRA allocator can leave reserved state behind when it stops considering a candidate device, which can make a schedulable pod fail to schedule.

`allocateDevice` reserves a device's shared counters and adds claim constraints before it may reject the candidate on a device taint or a claim constraint. title: DRA structured allocator counter caches are keyed by pool name and collide across drivers
description:
### What happened?

The structured DRA allocator scopes resource pools by both driver and pool name, but its shared-counter caches are keyed by the pool name alone.

When two different drivers publish pools with the same name on the same node, and devices in both pools consume counters, their counter accounting collides. Allocating a device from the first driver's pool can cause an otherwise available device from the second driver's independent pool to be rejected with `Insufficient counters`.
resolution: Closed via GitHub issue #140434 in kubernetes/kubernetes (see linked PR/comments for fix details)

title: ParentAwareNamingStrategy does not inspect grandparent application contexts
description:
## Summary

`ParentAwareNamingStrategy.parentContextContainsSameBean()` recursively advances a `context` parameter but obtains the next parent from `this.applicationContext` instead of that parameter. The first call is correct; on a three-or-more-level hierarchy, later calls keep checking the original immediate parent and never inspect the grandparent or higher ancestors.

title: Decouple cache_miss_wait_nanos from DIRECTORY_METRICS_FEATURE_FLAG
description: The `cache_miss_wait_nanos` header metric is currently gated behind `DIRECTORY_METRICS_FEATURE_FLAG`, but it can be released independently with a small change to `SearchService`/`DefaultSearchContext`/`fetch` paths. The metric is already recorded unconditionally on cache misses (`CacheMissHandler.record()`); the flag only gates whether it is surfaced in the response header. Decoupling it would allow the metric to be available in production without enabling the full flag overhead.
resolution: Closed via GitHub issue #155963 in elastic/elasticsearch (see linked PR/comments for fix details)

description:

`XSETID key <id> ENTRIESADDED n` lets you lower a stream's `entries_added`
counter. The command validates only that the new value is not smaller than the
current stream length; it does **not** reconcile it against the consumer
groups' `entries_read`. After `XTRIM` shrinks the stream, `entries_added` can
be set below a group's `entries_read`, breaking the invariant
`entries_read <= entries_added`.

This has two observable effects:

1. **Negative lag.** `XINFO GROUPS` reports
resolution: Closed via GitHub issue #15488 in redis/redis (see linked PR/comments for fix details)

title: AbortSignal.any(): observed composites still accumulate in a long-lived source's kDependantSignals after #62367 (not GC-pruned)
description:
Follow-up to #62363 / #62367.

#62367 ("defer `AbortSignal.any()` following") stops **listener-less** composites from following their sources eagerly. But a composite that **is** observed (has an `abort` listener) still follows its sources, and when one of those sources is **long-lived**, the composite's entry accumulates in that source's `kDependantSignals` and is **not pruned even by a forced `global.gc()`**. `size` grows monotonically for as long as the process runs.

Reproduces on **v24.18.0
resolution: Closed via GitHub issue #64476 in nodejs/node (see linked PR/comments for fix details)
